title: Coinsurance, conditions and claims
summary: Follow Tony's Detroit fire claim: the coinsurance math, his duties, the insurer's rights, lenders and bailees, and Michigan's claim rules.
objectives: Work a coinsurance problem in the right order, capped by the limit
Explain vacancy, duties after loss, assignment, abandonment and binders
Tell subrogation from salvage; know settlement options and the duty to defend
Contrast mortgagee, loss payee and bailee; know Michigan's claim rules

scenes.title: Fire at Tony's Pizza: coinsurance, conditions and claims
scenes.subtitle: One Detroit fire claim, start to finish: coinsurance, conditions, lenders and Michigan claim rules

beats.text: Meet Tony. His Detroit pizza shop is insured under the 2012 BPP, the Building and Personal Property form.
beats.say: Meet Tony. His Detroit pizza shop is insured under the twenty twelve B P P, the Building and Personal Property form.

beats.text: One November morning, a roofer's torch sets the roof on fire.
beats.say: One November morning, a roofer's torch sets the roof on fire.

scenes.title: The fire's out. Now what, Tony?
scenes.src: ISO CP 00 10 10 12 (2012 BPP), E.1 Abandonment, E.3 Duties; ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Cond. C; question core-042

draw.text: There's a hole in my roof!

beats.text: There's a hole in the roof, and rain is coming tonight. What does Tony do first?
beats.say: There's a hole in the roof, and rain is coming tonight. What does Tony do first?

options.label: Wait till spring, then call the insurer
options.fail: After a loss, the insured must give prompt notice. Calling months later breaks that duty.

beats.text: Tony calls in April. That's not the prompt notice the insured must give.
beats.say: Tony calls in April. That's not the prompt notice the insured must give.

draw.text: Hi! About that fire in November...

options.label: Leave the hole. The insurer will fix it.
options.fail: After a loss, the insured must protect the property from further damage, like covering a hole in the roof.

beats.text: Rain pours in all night. The insured must protect the property from further damage.
beats.say: Rain pours in all night. The insured must protect the property from further damage.

options.label: Leave the burnt oven at the insurer's door
options.fail: The insured can't force damaged property on the insurer: no abandonment. The insurer may choose to take it, but that's its call.

beats.text: Tony dumps his burnt oven at the insurer's door. Nope: no abandonment allowed.
beats.say: Tony dumps his burnt oven at the insurer's door. Nope: no abandonment allowed.

options.label: Tarp the roof, call the insurer, list damage
options.win: Prompt notice, protect the property, list the damage. If the insurer asks, send a sworn proof of loss within 60 days after its request.

beats.text: Smart. Tony tarps the hole, calls the insurer right away, and starts a damage list.
beats.say: Smart. Tony tarps the hole, calls the insurer right away, and starts a damage list.

reveal.text: Duties after a loss: prompt notice, police for theft, protect the property, and an inventory. If asked, a sworn proof of loss within 60 days. And no abandonment.
reveal.say: Duties after a loss: prompt notice, police for theft, protect the property, and an inventory. If asked, a sworn proof of loss within sixty days. And no abandonment.

scenes.title: Did Tony carry enough?
scenes.src: ISO CP 00 10 10 12 (2012 BPP), F.1 Coinsurance; memory hook mn_core-19
scenes.plain: Insure for at least a set share of the property's value, like 80%. Carry less, and every loss is paid short, in proportion.
scenes.example: Tony's building is worth $400,000 when the fire hits. At 80%, he should carry $320,000. He carries $240,000.
scenes.exam: Use the value at the time of loss, not when the policy began. Hook: Did over Should, times the Loss, minus the Deductible.

beats.text: Coinsurance: insure at least a set share of the property's value, like 80%. Carry less, and every loss gets paid short, in proportion.
beats.say: Coinsurance: insure at least a set share of the property's value, like eighty percent. Carry less, and every loss gets paid short, in proportion.

beats.text: Tony's building is worth $400,000 when the fire hits. At 80%, he should carry $320,000. He carries $240,000. So Should is $320,000, and Did is $240,000.
beats.say: Tony's building is worth four hundred thousand dollars when the fire hits. At eighty percent, he should carry three hundred twenty thousand dollars. He carries two hundred forty thousand dollars. So Should is three hundred twenty thousand dollars, and Did is two hundred forty thousand dollars.

beats.text: Use the value at the time of loss, not when the policy began. Hook: Did over Should, times the Loss, minus the Deductible.
beats.say: Use the value at the time of loss, not when the policy began. Hook: Did over Should, times the Loss, minus the Deductible.

scenes.title: Did over Should: Tony's $50,000 fire
scenes.src: ISO CP 00 10 10 12 (2012 BPP), F.1 Coinsurance and D Deductible; memory hook mn_core-19; questions core-039, core-040

goal.text: Find the smallest limit that pays Tony the whole $50,000 loss, minus only his $1,000 deductible.

beats.text: The fire did $50,000 of damage to the building. The deductible is $1,000.
beats.say: The fire did fifty thousand dollars of damage to the building. The deductible is one thousand dollars.

beats.text: Did over Should is 75%. Times the loss, that's $37,500.
beats.say: Did over Should is seventy-five percent. Times the loss, that's thirty-seven thousand five hundred dollars.

beats.text: The deductible comes off last: $36,500.
beats.say: The deductible comes off last: thirty-six thousand five hundred dollars.

beats.text: Your turn. Find the smallest limit with no penalty.
beats.say: Your turn. Find the smallest limit with no penalty.

reveal.text: $320,000. When Did meets Should, there's no penalty.
reveal.say: Three hundred twenty thousand dollars. When Did meets Should, there's no penalty.

reveal.text: And the limit still caps the payment: a total loss that computes above the limit pays just the limit.
reveal.say: And the limit still caps the payment: a total loss that computes above the limit pays just the limit.

scenes.q: A building worth $500,000 at the time of loss is insured for $300,000 with 80% coinsurance and a $1,000 deductible. A $100,000 covered loss occurs. What does the insurer pay?

beats.text: Quick check: a bakery nearby. What does the insurer pay?
beats.say: Quick check: a bakery nearby. What does the insurer pay?

reveal.say: Seventy-four thousand dollars. Should is eighty percent of five hundred thousand dollars, or four hundred thousand dollars. Three hundred thousand dollars divided by four hundred thousand dollars is zero point seven five.

reveal.text: So 75% of the loss is $75,000, minus the deductible: $74,000.
reveal.say: So seventy-five percent of the loss is seventy-five thousand dollars, minus the deductible: seventy-four thousand dollars.

reveal.text: Traps: $74,250 takes the deductible off first. $59,000 uses the full value, not 80%.
reveal.say: Traps: seventy-four thousand two hundred fifty dollars takes the deductible off first. Fifty-nine thousand dollars uses the full value, not eighty percent.

scenes.title: Tony's old shop: vacant or unoccupied?
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: vacant, unoccupied; confusion pair cp_personal-08; ISO CP 00 10 10 12 (2012 BPP), E.6.a, E.6.b
scenes.plain: Little or no furniture or belongings inside. The stuff is gone, not just the people.
scenes.example: Before selling his old east-side shop, Tony moved everything from it to the new one. It sat empty and unused, for sale.
scenes.exam: Unoccupied: people away, belongings still there, like a furnished house while its owners spend four months in Florida.

draw.text: 2012 BPP: vacant unless at least 31% of its square footage is in use

beats.text: Rewind to before Tony sold his old shop. Exam word: vacant, meaning little or no furniture or belongings inside. The stuff is gone, not just the people.
beats.say: Rewind to before Tony sold his old shop. Exam word: vacant, meaning little or no furniture or belongings inside. The stuff is gone, not just the people.

beats.text: He moved everything from his old east-side shop to the new one. It sat empty and unused, for sale.
beats.say: He moved everything from his old east-side shop to the new one. It sat empty and unused, for sale.

beats.text: Watch out: people away, but belongings still there? That's unoccupied, like a furnished house while its owners spend four months in Florida. Look for the stuff.
beats.say: Watch out: people away, but belongings still there? That's unoccupied, like a furnished house while its owners spend four months in Florida. Look for the stuff.

beats.text: The 2012 BPP has its own test: an owner's building is vacant unless at least 31% of its square footage is in use.
beats.say: The twenty twelve B P P has its own test: an owner's building is vacant unless at least thirty-one percent of its square footage is in use.

beats.text: Past 60 consecutive days vacant, losses such as vandalism, building glass breakage, water damage and theft aren't covered. Other covered losses are cut 15%.
beats.say: Past sixty consecutive days vacant, losses such as vandalism, building glass breakage, water damage and theft aren't covered. Other covered losses are cut fifteen percent.

scenes.title: Tony's empty shop, under the 2012 BPP
scenes.src: ISO CP 00 10 10 12 (2012 BPP), E.6.b Vacancy; question core-041

cards.text: Vacant 75 days: vandals spray-paint the walls.
cards.why: After more than 60 consecutive days vacant, vandalism isn't covered.

cards.text: Vacant 75 days: a windstorm tears off part of the roof.
cards.why: Windstorm isn't on the vacancy list, so it's paid, but reduced by 15%.

cards.text: Vacant 75 days: thieves steal the copper pipes.
cards.why: Vacant over 60 consecutive days: theft and attempted theft aren't covered.

cards.text: Vacant 40 days: a windstorm tears off part of the roof.
cards.why: The vacancy rule starts only after more than 60 consecutive days vacant.

cards.text: Vacant 75 days: a baseball smashes the shop's window.
cards.why: Vacant over 60 consecutive days: building glass breakage isn't covered.

cards.text: Vacant 75 days: lightning sets the roof on fire.
cards.why: Fire and lightning aren't on the vacancy list: paid, but cut by 15%.

beats.text: Your turn. The old shop had the same 2012 BPP. What happens to each loss?
beats.say: Your turn. The old shop had the same twenty twelve B P P. What happens to each loss?

reveal.text: Past 60 consecutive days, the listed perils are out; every other covered loss is cut 15%.
reveal.say: Past sixty consecutive days, the listed perils are out; every other covered loss is cut fifteen percent.

scenes.title: The insurer goes after the roofer
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: subrogation, salvage; questions core-044, core-bas-43
scenes.plain: Once the insurer pays you, it steps into your shoes and can recover from whoever is legally liable for the loss.
scenes.example: The insurer pays Tony for the fire. Then it sues the careless roofer whose torch started it, to get its money back.
scenes.exam: Don't mix it up with salvage: the damaged property left after a loss, like Tony's burnt oven.

beats.text: A careless roofer started Tony's fire. Subrogation: once the insurer pays Tony, it steps into his shoes. It takes over his right to recover from the party legally liable.
beats.say: A careless roofer started Tony's fire. Subrogation: once the insurer pays Tony, it steps into his shoes. It takes over his right to recover from the party legally liable.

beats.text: So it sues the roofer whose torch started the fire, to get its money back.
beats.say: So it sues the roofer whose torch started the fire, to get its money back.

beats.text: Not salvage: that's the damaged property left after a loss, like the burnt oven.
beats.say: Not salvage: that's the damaged property left after a loss, like the burnt oven.

scenes.title: Tony's policies: the fine print
scenes.src: ISO CP 00 10 10 12, E.4; ISO CP 00 90 07 88, E, F; ISO IL 00 17 11 98, F; ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. I A.1.a; IRMI glossary

spots.label: Settlement options
spots.text: 2012 BPP: the insurer chooses to pay the value, pay to repair or replace, take the property, or rebuild. It gives notice within 30 days after the sworn proof of loss.

spots.label: Salvage
spots.text: The burnt oven is salvage: damaged property left after the loss. The insurer may take it at an agreed or appraised value. Tony can't force it to.

spots.label: Liberalization
spots.text: If the insurer broadens this form without charging more premium, Tony's existing policy gets the broader coverage automatically.

spots.label: Duty to defend
spots.text: If a customer sues Tony for covered damages, his CGL insurer defends him. That duty ends when the limit is used up paying judgments or settlements.

spots.label: No benefit to bailee
spots.text: Movers hauling Tony's tables to the new shop for a fee can't benefit from his insurance. Same for a dry cleaner or a warehouse: his policy won't cover their liability.

spots.label: Assignment
spots.text: When Tony sold the old shop, he couldn't hand his policy to the buyer: transferring it needs the insurer's written consent.

beats.text: Now, Tony's fine print. Tap the six glowing spots.
beats.say: Now, Tony's fine print. Tap the six glowing spots.

reveal.text: The insurer picks how to settle and may take salvage. Liberalization: broader coverage at no extra premium applies automatically.
reveal.say: The insurer picks how to settle and may take salvage. Liberalization: broader coverage at no extra premium applies automatically.

reveal.text: Duty to defend: his CGL insurer defends suits for covered damages until the limit is used up paying judgments or settlements.
reveal.say: Duty to defend: his C G L insurer defends suits for covered damages until the limit is used up paying judgments or settlements.

reveal.text: No benefit to bailee: movers can't use his insurance. No assignment without written consent.
reveal.say: No benefit to bailee: movers can't use his insurance. No assignment without written consent.

scenes.title: Mortgagee or loss payee: two umbrellas
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11 (2011 HO), Sec. I Cond. L, S; IRMI glossary: loss payable clause; adapted from memory hook mn_core-21
scenes.hook: The mortgagee brings its own umbrella; a loss payee stands under yours.
items: Mortgage clause: pays the mortgagee and the insured as interests appear
Owner denied? Mortgagee collects if it reports changes, pays premium due and files a sworn statement
Loss payable: pays a party such as an equipment lessor, as its interest may appear
Typical loss payable clause: insured denied, the payee usually gets nothing

beats.text: A bank holding a home's mortgage is the mortgagee. The 2011 homeowners mortgage clause pays the mortgagee and the insured as interests appear. The mortgagee brings its own umbrella. Despite the owner's denial, it collects if it reports changes, pays premium due and files a sworn statement.
beats.say: A bank holding a home's mortgage is the mortgagee. The twenty eleven homeowners mortgage clause pays the mortgagee and the insured as interests appear. The mortgagee brings its own umbrella. Despite the owner's denial, it collects if it reports changes, pays premium due and files a sworn statement.

beats.text: A loss payee stands under yours. A loss payable clause pays a party such as an equipment lessor, as its interest may appear.
beats.say: A loss payee stands under yours. A loss payable clause pays a party such as an equipment lessor, as its interest may appear.

beats.text: Here, that's the company leasing Tony his fridge. But under a typical clause, if Tony is denied, the company usually gets nothing.
beats.say: Here, that's the company leasing Tony his fridge. But under a typical clause, if Tony is denied, the company usually gets nothing.

scenes.title: A Flint house burns: what does the bank do?
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11 (2011 HO), Sec. I Cond. L, S; IRMI glossary: loss payable clause; question core-045; confusion pair cp_personal-09

beats.text: In Flint, a homeowner burns his own house for the money. His 2011 homeowners claim is denied.
beats.say: In Flint, a homeowner burns his own house for the money. His twenty eleven homeowners claim is denied.

beats.text: We're the named mortgagee. What do we do?
beats.say: We're the named mortgagee. What do we do?
beats.speaker: Banker

options.label: Give up: his denial sinks us too
options.fail: Under the mortgage clause, the owner's denial doesn't wipe out the mortgagee's valid claim, if the mortgagee meets the conditions.

beats.text: The bank walks away. Wrong clause: that's how a typical loss payable clause works.
beats.say: The bank walks away. Wrong clause: that's how a typical loss payable clause works.

options.label: Sue the owner and win in court first
options.fail: No judgment is needed. The mortgagee collects by meeting the clause's conditions, like a sworn statement of loss within 60 days after notice.

beats.text: Two years in court later, the bank learns it never needed a judgment first.
beats.say: Two years in court later, the bank learns it never needed a judgment first.

options.label: File a sworn statement within 60 days
options.win: The mortgagee's claim stands if it reports known changes in risk, pays premium due on demand, and files a sworn statement within 60 days after notice.

beats.text: The bank reports what it knows, pays any premium due, and files a sworn statement within 60 days. Paid.
beats.say: The bank reports what it knows, pays any premium due, and files a sworn statement within sixty days. Paid.

reveal.text: Its own umbrella: the mortgagee collects despite the denial, if it meets the conditions.
reveal.say: Its own umbrella: the mortgagee collects despite the denial, if it meets the conditions.

scenes.title: Tony wants an expert on his side
scenes.src: MCL 500.1226(3), (4); IRMI glossary: adjuster, independent adjuster, public adjuster; memory hook mn_core-22; question core-049

beats.text: Three adjusters offer to help. Staff is on the insurer's Staff. Independent is Insurer-hired, on contract. Public is for the Policyholder, paid a Percentage.
beats.say: Three adjusters offer to help. Staff is on the insurer's Staff. Independent is Insurer-hired, on contract. Public is for the Policyholder, paid a Percentage.

beats.text: Who's on my side?
beats.say: Who's on my side?

options.label: The insurance company's staff adjuster
options.fail: A staff adjuster is the insurer's own employee. He works for the insurer, not for Tony.

beats.text: Tony asks the insurer's own staff adjuster to fight the insurer. Awkward: he's the insurer's employee.
beats.say: Tony asks the insurer's own staff adjuster to fight the insurer. Awkward: he's the insurer's employee.

options.label: Independent adjuster: "I'm not with them!"
options.fail: Independent means not on the insurer's payroll, not on your side: insurers hire independent adjusters on contract.

beats.text: Insurers hire him on contract. Independent of their payroll, but not on Tony's side.
beats.say: Insurers hire him on contract. Independent of their payroll, but not on Tony's side.

options.label: A public adjuster for a 10% fee
options.win: A public adjuster represents the insured. In Michigan: a written contract on a commissioner-approved form, and a fee of at most 10% of the settlement.

beats.text: Good call. A public adjuster works for Tony, not the insurer, under a written contract.
beats.say: Good call. A public adjuster works for Tony, not the insurer, under a written contract.

reveal.text: Only the public adjuster works for the policyholder, and Michigan caps the fee at 10%.
reveal.say: Only the public adjuster works for the policyholder, and Michigan caps the fee at ten percent.

scenes.title: Michigan puts the insurer on a clock
scenes.src: MCL 500.2006(3), (4) (timely payment of claims); MCL 500.2833(1)(p); questions core-050, core-051, prop-008

draw.label: What proof of loss it needs, in writing

draw.text: Interest starts 60 days after satisfactory proof of loss
Fire loss payable within 30 days after proof of the amount of loss

beats.text: In Michigan, within 30 days after getting the claim, the insurer must say in writing what proof of loss it needs, unless it settles first.
beats.say: In Michigan, within thirty days after getting the claim, the insurer must say in writing what proof of loss it needs, unless it settles first.

beats.text: Benefits not paid within 60 days after satisfactory proof of loss earn Tony 12% simple interest a year. The interest starts on day 60.
beats.say: Benefits not paid within sixty days after satisfactory proof of loss earn Tony twelve percent simple interest a year. The interest starts on day sixty.

beats.text: So they get 60 days to pay me?
beats.say: So they get sixty days to pay me?

beats.text: 60 days is the timely-payment deadline. But Michigan fire-policy law makes his fire loss payable within 30 days after proof of the amount of loss.
beats.say: Sixty days is the timely-payment deadline. But Michigan fire-policy law makes his fire loss payable within thirty days after proof of the amount of loss.

scenes.title: Tony buys the building next door
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: binder, representation, material misrepresentation, express authority; MCL 500.1201(h); question core-048
scenes.plain: Temporary evidence of insurance until the policy is issued.
scenes.example: Tony buys the building next door. Dana has binding authority, so she covers it that day with a binder: in writing, with an end date, naming the insurer.
scenes.exam: Actual authority: granted by the insurer. Apparent: what a reasonable person assumes from how the insurer presents her. A license alone gives neither.

beats.text: Tony buys the building next door. Dana covers it that day with a binder: temporary evidence of insurance until the policy is issued.
beats.say: Tony buys the building next door. Dana covers it that day with a binder: temporary evidence of insurance until the policy is issued.

beats.text: Dana can do that because she has binding authority. A binder should be in writing, have a definite time limit, and name the insurer.
beats.say: Dana can do that because she has binding authority. A binder should be in writing, have a definite time limit, and name the insurer.

beats.text: Dana binds only within her actual or apparent authority. Actual authority is granted by the insurer.
beats.say: Dana binds only within her actual or apparent authority. Actual authority is granted by the insurer.

beats.text: Apparent authority is what a reasonable person assumes from how the insurer presents her. A license alone gives neither.
beats.say: Apparent authority is what a reasonable person assumes from how the insurer presents her. A license alone gives neither.

beats.text: Tony's application answers are representations, statements he believes are true. A material misrepresentation can void coverage.
beats.say: Tony's application answers are representations, statements he believes are true. A material misrepresentation can void coverage.

2012 BPP, vacant over 60 days: some perils out, the rest cut 15%
Subrogation: after paying, the insurer recovers from the party liable
A mortgagee can collect after a denial; a loss payee usually can't
Michigan: 12%/yr on insureds' late benefits; public adjusters max 10%

beats.say: A mortgagee can collect after a denial; a loss payee usually can't.

beats.text: Next time, I'm carrying enough insurance.
beats.say: Next time, I'm carrying enough insurance.
